mainTopic: Betrothal on condition of no vows or blemishes, and the משנה about remarrying a wife divorced because of a vow
overview: First the גמרא finishes the earlier discussion: the girl may do מיאון and leave. Then a ברייתא teaches that if a man betroths a woman on condition that she has no vows, and a חכם later releases her vows, she is betrothed. If the condition was no blemishes and a doctor heals her, she is not betrothed. The reason is that a חכם uproots the vow from the start, while a doctor heals only from now on. A second ברייתא says that even with the חכם she is not betrothed. רבא explains that the first ברייתא follows רבי מאיר, who holds a man does not mind his wife being embarrassed in בית דין. The second follows רבי אלעזר, who holds he does mind. The גמרא shows the source of this argument in a משנה about a man who divorced his wife because of a vow, where רבי יהודה, רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר each say when he may take her back. Finally the גמרא asks for רבי יהודה's reason and begins to quote a פסוק, which comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Ending of the earlier case: she may refuse and leave
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of the previous discussion: the girl may do מיאון and go on her way.
steps.simpleTranslation: She may refuse and go on her way.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes the discussion from the previous page. The girl may refuse her husband through מיאון and simply leave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ruling treats the marriage as never really taking hold, because the קידושין was based on a mistake. She leaves without a גט, through מיאון.

keyTerms.meaning: She refuses (does מיאון, the way a girl married as a minor can leave the marriage)
And she goes on her way (leaves with no גט)

phrases.english: She refuses and goes on her way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion carried over from the previous page.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Because the marriage was based on a mistake, she may do מיאון and leave.

steps.title: A sage's release saves the betrothal, a doctor's cure does not
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: if a חכם releases her vows she is betrothed, but if a doctor heals her blemishes she is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: If she went to a sage and he released her vows, she is betrothed. If she went to a doctor and he healed her, she is not betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא about a man who betrothed a woman on a condition that turned out to be false. If a חכם then cancels her vows, the קידושין stands. If a doctor heals her blemish, it does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases the problem is fixed after the betrothal. Even so, the ברייתא gives them opposite results. That difference is exactly what the next step asks about.

keyTerms.meaning: A Torah sage who can release vows
He released her (cancelled her vows)
Doctor
She is betrothed (the קידושין is valid)

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
If she went to a sage and he released her [vows], she is betrothed.
phrases.notes: The case assumed here: he betrothed her on condition that she had no vows, and it turned out she did.

phrases.aramaic: אֵצֶל רוֹפֵא וְרִיפֵּא אוֹתָהּ — אֵינָהּ מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת.
phrases.english: If she went to a doctor and he healed her, she is not betrothed.
phrases.notes: Here the condition was that she had no blemishes.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָלְכָה אֵצֶל חָכָם וְהִתִּירָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: fixing the problem after a conditional betrothal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Release by a חכם makes her betrothed; healing by a doctor does not.

steps.title: What is the difference between a sage and a doctor?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks why the חכם and the doctor are treated differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between a sage and a doctor?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a clarifying question to set up its explanation. In both cases the problem was fixed, so why are the results different?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack on the ruling. It is a request for the reasoning behind it, and the next step gives the answer.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between

phrases.english: What is the difference between a sage and a doctor?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the ruling in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does a חכם's release save the קידושין while a doctor's healing does not?

steps.title: A sage uproots from the start, a doctor heals only from now
steps.stepSummary: A חכם cancels the vow back to its beginning, while a doctor's cure only works from now on.
steps.simpleTranslation: A sage uproots the vow from its very start, but a doctor heals only from now onward.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question. A חכם's release reaches back in time, but a doctor's healing does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a חכם releases a vow, it is as if she never vowed. So at the moment of קידושין she had no vows, and the condition was met. A doctor only fixes the blemish from now on, so at the time of קידושין she did have a blemish and the condition failed.

keyTerms.meaning: Uproots
From its root, from the very start
From here onward, from now on

steps.whatToRemember: התרת נדרים by a חכם works backwards to the start, and healing works only from now on. That is why one saves the קידושין and the other does not.

phrases.english: A sage uproots the vow from its very start,

phrases.aramaic: וְרוֹפֵא אֵינוֹ מְרַפֵּא אֶלָּא מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא.
phrases.english: but a doctor heals only from here onward.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A חכם's release works backwards, so she never had a vow at the time of קידושין; healing works only going forward.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that התרת נדרים works backwards is a basic principle that comes up in many places.

steps.title: Another ברייתא says even the sage's release does not help
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא rules that in both cases, sage and doctor, she is not betrothed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: If she went to a sage and he released her, or to a doctor and he healed her, she is not betrothed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first ברייתא with a second one. The second one says the חכם's release does not save the קידושין either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא said a release by a חכם makes her betrothed. The second treats the חכם just like the doctor: no קידושין. The two sources contradict each other on the חכם case.

phrases.english: But it was taught:
If she went to a sage and he released her,
or to a doctor and he healed her,
she is not betrothed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contradicts the ruling of step 2 on the חכם case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first ברייתא's ruling that a חכם's release makes her betrothed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two ברייתות give opposite rulings for the same case of a חכם releasing her vows.

steps.title: רבא: the two ברייתות follow רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the ברייתות reflect a מחלוקת: does a man mind his wife being embarrassed in בית דין?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This is no difficulty. One ברייתא follows רבי מאיר and the other follows רבי אלעזר. The first follows רבי מאיר, who said a man does not mind his wife being embarrassed in court. The second follows רבי אלעזר, who said a man does not want his wife to be embarrassed in court.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא resolves the contradiction by assigning each ברייתא to a different תנא. The real question is whether the husband would accept her going to בית דין to have her vow released.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי מאיר, the husband does not mind her going to court, so the חכם's release counts and she is betrothed (the first ברייתא). According to רבי אלעזר, the husband does not want her shamed in court, so a release that requires going there does not satisfy him. So she is not betrothed (the second ברייתא).

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (introduces an answer)
This one… that one (pointing to two sources)
That she be embarrassed or disgraced
Court, here where a חכם releases vows

steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions agree that a חכם's release works backwards. The argument is only about whether the husband is happy with her going to בית דין to get it.
steps.whatToRemember: The first ברייתא (she is betrothed) follows רבי מאיר: a man does not mind. The second (she is not) follows רבי אלעזר: a man does mind.

phrases.english: Rava said: It is not difficult,

phrases.aramaic: הָא — רַבִּי מֵאִיר, הָא — רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר.
phrases.english: this one follows Rabbi Meir, and that one follows Rabbi Elazar.
phrases.notes: The first "this" is the ברייתא where she is betrothed; the second is the one where she is not.

phrases.english: This one follows Rabbi Meir, who said:

phrases.aramaic: אָדָם רוֹצֶה שֶׁתִּתְבַּזֶּה אִשְׁתּוֹ בְּבֵית דִּין.
phrases.english: A man is willing for his wife to be embarrassed in court.
That one follows Rabbi Elazar, who said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אָדָם רוֹצֶה שֶׁתִּתְבַּזֶּה אִשְׁתּוֹ בְּבֵית דִּין.
phrases.english: A man is not willing for his wife to be embarrassed in court.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning each source to a different תנא (תנאי היא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות seemed to give opposite rulings on one case under a single view.
steps.terutzMaskana: They reflect a מחלוקת between רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר about whether a man minds his wife being embarrassed in בית דין.

steps.title: Where is this disagreement found?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the מחלוקת between רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר is taught.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the argument רבא just mentioned. This sets up the quotation of a משנה in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא described the two views but did not say where they appear. The גמרא wants the original text in which they argue.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? (asking for the source)

phrases.english: What is it?
phrases.notes: Meaning: where do רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר argue about this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the views cited in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source text of the מחלוקת between רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר.

steps.title: The משנה about divorcing because of a vow or a bad name
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting a משנה: a man who divorced his wife because of a vow or a bad name may not take her back.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: One who divorces his wife because of a vow may not take her back. Because of a bad name, he may not take her back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts answering by quoting the משנה where the argument appears. This part only gives the opening rules, and the views of the תנאים come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a man who divorced his wife over a vow or a bad reputation can never remarry her. The argument between רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר about the vow case is found in the continuation of this משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: One who divorces his wife
He may not take her back
A bad name or reputation

phrases.english: As we learned:

phrases.aramaic: הַמּוֹצִיא אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ מִשּׁוּם נֶדֶר — לֹא יַחְזִיר.
phrases.english: One who divorces his wife because of a vow may not take her back.
Because of a bad name, he may not take her back.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: הַמּוֹצִיא אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ מִשּׁוּם נֶדֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering step 7 by quoting the source משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is the משנה in גיטין about divorcing a wife because of a vow or a bad name. The quote continues beyond this point.

steps.title: The quoted משנה continues: the views of רבי יהודה and רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה: if many people knew about the vow, he may not remarry her, and if not, he may. רבי מאיר: if the vow needs a חכם, he may not remarry her, and if not, he may.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: any vow that many people know about, he may not take her back. If many people do not know about it, he may take her back. רבי מאיר says: any vow that needs a חכם to look into it, he may not take her back. If it does not need a חכם to look into it, he may take her back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the משנה it started in step 8. Here we hear the first two opinions on when a man may remarry a wife he divorced because of her vow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה draws the line by whether the vow was known to many people. רבי מאיר draws it by whether a חכם is needed to release the vow, or whether the husband can cancel it himself. These are two different ways of deciding the same question.

keyTerms.meaning: Many people, the public
He may not take her back (remarry her)
A sage's investigation, needed to release some vows
A vow

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two opinions. רבי יהודה asks how many people knew about the vow. רבי מאיר asks who is able to release it: a חכם, or the husband himself.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Any vow that many people knew about —
he may not take her back.
If many people did not know about it —
he may take her back.
Rabbi Meir says:
Any vow that needs a sage's investigation —
he may not take her back.
And one that does not need a sage's investigation —
he may take her back.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: כׇּל נֶדֶר שֶׁיָּדְעוּ בּוֹ רַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quotation of the משנה begun in step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה's opinions: רבי יהודה (public versus private vow) and רבי מאיר (vow that needs a חכם versus one that does not).

steps.title: רבי אלעזר forbids both cases and explains why
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says that in both of רבי מאיר's cases he may not take her back. He adds that the case that needs a חכם was forbidden only because of the case that does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: whether the vow needs a חכם or does not need one, he may not take her back. רבי אלעזר said: they forbade the case that needs a חכם only because of the case that does not need one.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the part of the משנה the גמרא was looking for in step 7. Here רבי אלעזר disagrees with רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר allowed remarriage when no חכם is needed. רבי אלעזר forbids it in that case too. He also explains that the case where no חכם is needed is the main reason for the rule, and the case that needs a חכם was forbidden because of it. This is the מחלוקת that רבא said lies behind the two ברייתות.

keyTerms.meaning: Both the case that needs a חכם and the case that does not
They did not forbid (together with אֶלָּא that follows: they forbade only because of)
Because of

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: only a vow that needs a חכם blocks remarriage. רבי אלעזר: both kinds block it, and the vow that needs no חכם is the main reason for the rule.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source of the רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר מחלוקת that רבא used in step 6 to explain why the two ברייתות disagree.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:
Both one that needs and one that does not need —
phrases.notes: He means a vow that needs a sage's investigation and one that does not.

phrases.english: he may not take her back.
Rabbi Elazar said:
They did not forbid the one that needs [a sage]
except because of the one that does not need [a sage].

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: אֶחָד צָרִיךְ וְאֶחָד אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion to רבי מאיר's view from step 9, which completes the source asked for in step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אלעזר forbids remarriage in both cases, and says the case needing a חכם was forbidden only because of the case that needs none.

steps.title: What is רבי יהודה's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source behind רבי יהודה's rule about a public vow and starts to quote a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי יהודה? As it is written:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks why רבי יהודה treats a vow known to many people differently. It begins to answer with a פסוק, and the פסוק itself comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's rule rests on how many people knew about the vow. The גמרא wants a source for why that makes a difference. The word דכתיב tells us a פסוק is about to be brought as proof.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
As it is written (a פסוק is coming)

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda?
As it is written:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: With the משנה now fully quoted, the גמרא goes back to explain the first opinion in it, רבי יהודה's.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source and reasoning for רבי יהודה's rule that a vow known to many people blocks remarriage.
